African Playhouse

A digital collection of games from African traditions, including Songo, Oware, Fanorona and Morabaraba, implemented from named rule editions and playable against the computer, on one device or at private online tables.

Visit the site ↗How to useEngineering record

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Designed the game collection and its multiplayer model: rule engines for traditional board games, a computer opponent at three levels, and private online tables on Supabase Realtime with guest sessions.

Solo and local games never touch the network. For an online table, the host gets an anonymous Supabase session without email, creates a private table and shares an invitation; moves travel over a Realtime channel and each client validates them with the same rule engine.

Key engineering decisions

01

Named rule editions

Rules differ between communities, so each implementation is a documented edition (Songo, Oware, Fanorona, Morabaraba) rather than a claimed canonical form.

02

Guests before accounts

Anonymous sessions remove sign-up friction for a casual game while still giving the server an identity for each seat.

Notes for reviewers

Limits and next stepsMove move validation to the server for ranked play, and finish online testing before enabling live payments.
01

Problem statement

Songo, Oware, Fanorona and Morabaraba are played across the continent yet are rarely available in careful digital form. Their rules vary between regions and sources, and families spread across several countries have few simple ways to play together.

02

Contribution

Thirteen games are playable: eight adaptations of widely known formats (Ludo Afrique, Yatzy Afrique, Dames d’Afrique, Snakes & Ladders Afrique, Tic-Tac-Toe Afrique, Water Sort Afrique, African Match Garden, and African Empires, a solo campaign set in a fictional Mali of 1325) and five traditional games (Songo, Oware, Naija Shapes, Fanorona and Morabaraba). Four traditional games follow an explicitly named edition, so the variant implemented can be identified. Eleven further traditions, from Bao to Diketo, are listed with their region and planned rules. Decorative boards, dice and tokens sold in the atelier never alter rules or probabilities.

03

Architecture

A React client hosted on Netlify. Supabase provides guest sessions without email, accounts, and real-time synchronisation for private tables. Solo and local games need no account and save their state on the device.

04

Verification and limitations

This is a test version: online tables are still being tested and payments run in test mode only. Rules of traditional games differ between communities; the named editions document which variant is implemented and make no claim to a canonical form.
